evidence_items.title: AdAstraAbyssoque/accelerate-bench
evidence_items.summary: Accelerate Bench asks whether coding agents can make whole scientific applications faster without breaking them. This dataset holds the 32 tasks of v1.1, the version evaluated in the paper, as Harbor task packages. Commit-derived tasks (left, as in GSO) start from one known performance commit and measure the agent's patch against it. Accelerate Bench tasks (right) fix the workload and the computation that must be preserved; the agent decides where and how to optimize, and… See the full description on the dataset page: https://huggingface.co/datasets/AdAstraAbyssoque/accelerate-bench.

evidence_items.title: Henard224/Drone-PUR-Benchmark
evidence_items.summary: Drone-PUR Benchmark Paper | Project This package provides the test split of Drone-PUR, covering perception, understanding, and reasoning in UAV scenes: 11 tasks, 20,051 test questions, and 22,248 image files. The ten choice-based tasks, including binary CJ, contain 18,431 questions; OD uses open-ended multi-box prediction. Images come from eight established datasets: VisDrone, DroneVehicle, DroneCrowd, MDMT, MDOT, DroneRGBT, AnimalDrone, and DroneBird. evidence_items.title: chocokiddo/DICE-Bench
evidence_items.summary: DICE-Bench: A Benchmark for Intervention-Aware AI Tutoring DICE-Bench is a mathematical tutoring benchmark introduced in DICE: Decoupling Capability from Intervention Necessity in LLM Tutoring (NeurIPS 2026). Most conversational tutoring datasets focus on what a tutor should say next. DICE-Bench addresses a complementary question: When does a student actually need intervention, and when should the tutor allow them to continue independently?
